title: Mixture-seq StressGrid: reproducible multi-GPU throughput fingerprinting for TP/PP meshes
creator: Ava Morales
description:
Goal: Build a reproducible, portable benchmark harness (StressGrid) that fingerprints throughput and latency characteristics for multi-GPU TP/PP inference clusters using mixture-of-sequence-length workloads. This ticket covers harness design, reference workloads, data collection pipeline, and a regression detector that can be wired into CI and the observability stack.

Scope:
- Support heterogeneous node shapes (e.g., 4xA100-80GB, 8xH100-80GB) and mixed PP/TP configs.
- Workloads: synthetic uniform seqlen runs, and mixture-of-seqlen traces derived from production sampling (short/med/long ratios).
- Metrics collected: tokens/sec (global and per-GPU), p50/p90/p95/p99 latency of first token and tail tokens, KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization, memory headroom, IPC, PCIe/NCCL bandwidth counters, and kernel-level timing.
- Regression detector: control-chart + Bayesian change-point alerts with bootstrap baseline; emit signal if steady-state tokens/sec drops >5% with p95 increase >15% after accounting for variance.
- Outputs: downloadable artifacts (time-series CSVs), dashboard templates, and a GitHub PR that runs a lightweight suite on nightly hardware smoke runs.
acceptance_criteria: StressGrid can run on a 4-GPU and 8-GPU cluster reproducibly (same config yields tokens/sec within 5% across three 30-min steady-state runs)
Seqlen-mixture runner reproduces observed production tail characteristics (p95 within 10% of sampled production traces for identical model+prompt mix)
Regression detector integrated to nightly CI: false positive rate <2% over a 30-day baseline and true positive detection of injected 10% throughput regressions in synthetic delta runs
Artifacts (CSV, perf profiles), dashboards, and a docs PR are published in drive/confluence and linked from the ticket
description_of_work: Planned work includes: 1) implement workload generator that accepts mixture definitions (e.g., 60% seqlen 64, 30% seqlen 512, 10% seqlen 2048) and produces arrival patterns (Poisson, bursty microburst). 2) Add synchronized KV warmup step to ensure steady-state starts with representative cache state. 3) Instrument per-step timings and GPU counters using nvtx/perf APIs and flush to time-series backend. 4) Implement regression-detector microservice that consumes aggregated run artifacts and applies control charts + Bayesian detection. 5) Create dashboards (Grafana) and an infra job template for nightly smoke runs. 6) Iterate on noise-reduction knobs (clock governors, NUMA pinning, NCCL tuning) to reduce variance for CI-run qualification.
progress_updates: 2026-02-11: PoC runner prototype implemented. Can launch mixture-of-seqlen workloads across a 4xA100 cluster and collect tokens/sec at 1s granularity. Initial variance observed ~12% between runs (target 5%).

2026-02-13: Root-cause analysis: variance dominated by inter-node clock governor differences and un-synced CPU frequency scaling. Added CPU governor pinning and isolated NIC interrupts. Variance dropped to ~6.8% on subsequent runs.

2026-02-15: Integrated NVTX spans and basic nvprof counters. Discovered periodic NCCL allreduce stalls correlated with background telemetry cronjob. Created ENG-287659 to gate cronjobs during benchmark windows.

2026-02-17: Implemented control-chart detector prototype (EWMA with bootstrap CI) and ran injected-delta experiments. Detector flagged a 7% throughput drop consistently; tuned sensitivity to reduce false alarms by increasing sample window for steady-state detection.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Hardware noise (thermal throttling, background services) inflates variance. Mitigation: standardized node prep script that pins clocks, disables non-essential daemons, and runs a thermal pre-warm sequence.
Risk: Production traces may contain PII or proprietary prompts. Mitigation: use sampled metadata (length, token-type mix) to synthesize privacy-preserving mixtures rather than copying raw prompts.
Risk: Regression detector overfitting to specific hardware. Mitigation: train baseline distributions per-cluster-type and include cross-cluster normalization factors.
